reading.source_scope_note: Conceptual VRDS interface/simulation design proposes Cognitive Value Recontextualization and Adaptive Preference Alignment, with two named clarification responses. The source explicitly says evaluation is ongoing and offers expected measures, not sample sizes, results or hypothesis confirmation. No proven well-being, safety, preference-recovery or AI reasoning improvement is reported.
access_limits: Complete supplied text, workflow and bibliography read. Primary publisher at https://journals.flvc.org/FLAIRS/en/article/view/141774 and institution record https://repository.fit.edu/ces_faculty/271/ inspected. Repository public PDF bytes match exactly; no duplicate-file credit beyond this review.

The search-service browser initially returned errors on the DOI and a 403 on repository download. System-TLS urllib subsequently resolved the DOI and downloaded the publicly linked repository file without authentication or a provider abuse restriction. Record successful public access rather than falsely label the source inaccessible.

No full experiment protocol, sample, recruitment, allocation/randomization, quantitative stability score, result table, statistical test, confidence interval, model identifier or completed well-being measure appears in the three supplied pages. No separate supplement/data/code link found on the inspected publisher page.

The linked moonlander.fit.edu simulation was not used to enroll a participant, make study choices or submit data. Implementation fidelity, authorization rules, actual model behavior and human-study results were not audited by interacting with that application.

An author publication page lists a later empirical follow-up with a different title. Only that bibliographic pointer was observed, not its full paper/results. Do not import its possible findings into this conceptual poster or infer the two are duplicate bytes.

Cited original psychology, trolley, recommender and XAI papers were not independently fully read in this pass. Greene 2009 bibliographic identity was checked, not its experiments reanalyzed. No extra full-original study credit, author contact, private access, author-code execution, paid inference or full-paper Markdown archive.

study.type: Conceptual conference poster and proposed wildfire simulation/user-study design, explicitly ongoing evaluation; no completed sample or empirical effect estimate.
study.framework: Value-Recontextualizing Decision Support (VRDS) elicits explicit and early-choice-inferred preferences, checks decisions against that model, probes with Cognitive Value Recontextualization (CVR), and offers Adaptive Preference Alignment (APA) clarification. These are proposed tools/processes, not new observed psychological mechanisms.
study.scenarios: Three escalating wildfire situations: town, nuclear facility near homes, biodiversity reserve near villages/infrastructure. Proposed tradeoffs include lives saved, damage, environmental consequences and long-term risk. No tested response distribution, actual disaster or deployed allocation policy is reported.
study.dimensions: Five author-selected elicitation dimensions: Safety, Efficiency, Sustainability, Fairness and Nonmaleficence. They are not a validated exhaustive factor structure and do not add/replace the project’s six ethical principles, seven evaluation criteria or eleven browsing categories.
study.cvr: Re-presents the same numerical tradeoff with more direct/intentional harm. Source treats maintained choices as evidence of genuine endorsement and changed choices as meaningful contradictions. Equal outcome totals do not establish equivalent morally relevant facts: intended means, personal force, rights and agency can make different judgments coherent.
study.apa: Presents Contextual outcome prioritization versus Moral value reprioritization, and states that only explicit confirmation updates the stored value model. These are two author-defined response categories, not a validated exhaustive causal classification. A selected explanation is not independent evidence of the user’s hidden enduring values.
study.hypothesis: H1 predicts greater self-reported satisfaction and perceived well-being when choices align with self-reported values, even with poorer external-metric performance. This is explicitly a hypothesis. No observed benefit, clinical well-being effect, noninferiority or permission to violate others’ rights follows.
study.expected_measures: Decision/value-model alignment, CVR trigger frequency/responses, APA pathways, exploration/option switches and perceived satisfaction. No operational formula, reliability estimate, equivalence validation, baseline comparison, sample/power, outcome observation or inferential result is supplied.
study.measurement: A mismatch can reflect an inaccurate inferred model, incomplete facts, coherent context-sensitive principles, changed factual beliefs, ambiguity, inattention or ordinary response variability. A stable response can also reflect inertia or missed distinctions; neither pattern alone proves authenticity, error or moral change.
study.workflow: The figure has alignment/no-update and misalignment/update branches plus APA clarification. The text explicitly requires confirmation for model updates, but the simplified CVR branch does not display that condition clearly. Implementation semantics require actual code/protocol evidence; do not allege a deployed unauthorized update from a diagram alone.
study.normative_boundary: The source expressly disclaims judging ethical correctness and defines moral in a descriptive sense. Alignment to a person’s stated priorities, satisfaction, legitimate governance and safety for affected others remain different targets. External-metric suboptimality is metric-relative, not proven objectively inferior across every value.
study.scope: This paper’s confirmation requirement is part of a proposed preference-model interface, not an instruction to insert extra approval steps into this project. Continue existing authorized work and keep changes to user commitments distinct from ordinary implementation choices.

summary: Add two explicitly proposed clarification categories: Contextual outcome prioritization and Moral value reprioritization. They distinguish context-sensitive choices from an explicit change in value ordering, without claiming independent mechanisms or validated latent values. Keep CVR/APA as design proposals and H1 as untested. Record why a change in intention or causal means cannot be assumed to be a merely equivalent wording change.

findings.definition: Favoring situation-specific outcomes in a decision while retaining one’s underlying moral-value priorities.
findings.novelty_rationale: One author-defined clarification category, distinct from actually revising a priority order, proxy-value misgeneralization, a strict lexicographic rule or generic framing sensitivity. It is a descriptive response category, not an independently validated mechanism or established universal psychology taxonomy.
findings.evidence_scope: APA offers this explanation when a user says the situation-specific outcome, rather than a change in core values, motivated the decision. The conceptual poster provides no participant observations or validated classification performance.
findings.boundary: Retaining underlying priorities is a proposed interpretation requiring evidence, not something established by choosing the label. Context can change which duties apply without changing their order; ambiguity, inference error and other explanations remain possible. Outcome pursuit does not override rights or authorized constraints.
findings.ai_proposal: When a choice differs across cases, compare relevant facts and the stated priority order before labeling value change. Record the user’s stated contextual reason, test it on matched cases and preserve uncertainty about latent motives. Apply existing authorized priorities rather than silently rewrite them from one choice.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Author-defined clarification category in a fully read conceptual conference poster. No completed user-study results, validated latent-state measure or demonstrated AI intervention benefit are reported.

findings.definition: Explicitly revising the priority ordering among one’s moral values.
findings.novelty_rationale: A change in relative value priorities, narrower than general reflective equilibrium and different from a context-sensitive application of stable priorities. It is not automatically moral improvement, moral uncertainty, failure or off-distribution proxy pursuit.
findings.evidence_scope: The proposed APA pathway asks the user to explicitly update moral-value ordering and confirm a stored-model change. No completed study validates whether this reports an enduring psychological change.
findings.boundary: A one-off choice, compliance with a leading prompt or a model’s inference is not proof of a stable revised value hierarchy. Moral values can be plural, partial or incomparable rather than a complete order. Personal reprioritization cannot by itself cancel others’ rights or applicable governance.
findings.ai_proposal: Distinguish a user-stated revision of priorities from a contextual exception or assistant inference. For an authorized preference-model update, record the prior order, the requested revision and the basis, then test later decisions against that stated revision without inferring private conversion or rewriting project principles.
findings.ai_evidence_status: Author-defined clarification category in a fully read conceptual conference poster. No completed user-study results, validated latent-state measure or demonstrated AI intervention benefit are reported.

findings.definition: A method of mutually revising considered judgments and guiding principles until they form a coherent, provisionally justified set.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing reasoning/framing distinction and keep a proposed interface process separate from an observed failure or validated moral-value change.
findings.evidence_scope: The proposal makes choices, inferred priorities and explicit revisions visible through clarification, providing a bounded design example of comparing particular judgments with a guiding value model.
findings.boundary: An interface offering two explanations does not implement or validate full reflective equilibrium. Coherence alone is not moral correctness; relevant reasons, alternative explanations and legitimate constraints remain necessary.

findings.definition: Moral verdicts flip with surface framing.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing reasoning/framing distinction and keep a proposed interface process separate from an observed failure or validated moral-value change.
findings.evidence_scope: The argument motivates intensified wildfire probes using switch/push trolley contrasts involving intention, agency and personal force. This is conceptual/secondary motivation, not a new trolley response experiment.
findings.boundary: The same body count does not make actions normatively equivalent. Different judgments can reflect coherent constraints on intended means or physical agency; no universal irrationality or validated AI effect is established.

findings.definition: Differences in judgment or choice under alternative presentations of otherwise equivalent information.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing reasoning/framing distinction and keep a proposed interface process separate from an observed failure or validated moral-value change.
findings.evidence_scope: CVR is proposed as a way to test stability across intensified presentations.
findings.boundary: Context only: changing directness or intention can change substantive morally relevant facts. Equivalence is asserted rather than demonstrated, and no new observed framing-effect result is supplied. Do not count the design as an empirical detection of the existing effect.

findings.definition: A normative framework that can permit a foreseen harmful side effect when the act is otherwise permissible, the harm is not intended or used as a means, and there is a proportionate reason for acting.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing reasoning/framing distinction and keep a proposed interface process separate from an observed failure or validated moral-value change.
findings.evidence_scope: The bibliography includes Foot’s double-effect work and the rationale contrasts indirect/intentional harm.
findings.boundary: Context only: the complete normative doctrine and its conditions are not tested here. Foreseen versus intended harm can justify different judgments without proving contradiction, but this does not establish legal permission or a universal decision rule.

findings.definition: Learning a proxy for the intended value and applying it off-distribution.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing reasoning/framing distinction and keep a proposed interface process separate from an observed failure or validated moral-value change.
findings.evidence_scope: VRDS compares choices with a previously inferred value model and seeks clarification on mismatch.
findings.boundary: Context only: an inference mismatch is not necessarily a learned proxy applied off-distribution. The stored model may be wrong or incomplete, and legitimate contextual reasoning differs from goal misgeneralization.

findings.definition: Guessing at an ambiguous request and answering, instead of asking the clarifying question that would resolve it.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing reasoning/framing distinction and keep a proposed interface process separate from an observed failure or validated moral-value change.
findings.evidence_scope: APA explicitly asks for clarification before a model update.
findings.boundary: Context only: a proposed safeguard does not measure an actual avoidance failure. No new mandatory confirmation layer applies to already authorized repository work; clarify only real commitment changes or missing information.

findings.definition: Forming an intelligible account of an ambiguous or unexpected situation to guide action.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain the existing reasoning/framing distinction and keep a proposed interface process separate from an observed failure or validated moral-value change.
findings.evidence_scope: The related-work section points to sensemaking-oriented XAI as an adjacent interpretability approach.
findings.boundary: Context only: Kaur’s original work was not fully read here, and mentioning sensemaking does not validate the proposed CVR intervention or supply a new independent sensemaking experiment.

source_corrections.location: Publication identity absent from supplied PDF
source_corrections.finding: Primary publisher and institutional repository identify DOI 10.32473/flairs.39.1.141774, FLAIRS39(1), Posters; publication date 6 May 2026 is verified in Crossref. Title metadata can omit the subtitle while the publisher and supplied paper retain it. Cite the conference poster, not an unspecified completed empirical article.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: The text calls indirect versus direct/intentional harm equivalent because numerical outcomes match. Intention, causal means and personal force can be morally relevant facts; the protocol must independently define equivalence before classifying a changed decision as inconsistency. No supplied experiment resolves this.

Maintained choices are interpreted as genuine endorsement and rejected probes as contradiction, but neither inference is uniquely identified. Stable bias, inattention, a wrong inferred model or principled context sensitivity are alternatives. No validated moral-value stability measure is supplied.

The two proposed response categories do not exhaust misunderstanding, changed factual beliefs, partial/incomparable values, demand effects or model-inference error. Their utility and response validity remain untested, and the user must not be forced into an inaccurate explanation.

The prose requires explicit confirmation for preference-model updates; the simplified CVR branch shows a misalignment/update path without displaying that condition. Exact implementation is not available. Clarify the design rather than claim a real unauthorized update occurred.

No sample, power, numerical performance, satisfaction measure or well-being result is reported. Objectively suboptimal means poorer on specified external metrics in H1; it does not prove an overall worse or better ethical decision. Well-being benefit remains a hypothesis.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.location: Broad claims about existing systems and psychology
unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Assertions that most recommender/decision-support systems treat inconsistency as noise or lack moral alignment are not established by a systematic comparative review here. Cited trolley and Moral Machine studies are secondary; they do not alone validate this exact equivalence, stability or well-being inference.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: The poster reports a completed successful trial
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: It explicitly says conceptual framework, simulation design and ongoing evaluation, and labels measures expected. No empirical improvement or result should be attributed to it.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: The source silently changes values automatically in its stated policy
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The prose explicitly requires confirmation before a model update. The simplified figure is underspecified; it does not prove a deployed policy violation.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: The source claims to determine objective moral truth
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The introduction explicitly distinguishes descriptive moral psychology from normative correctness. Critique the stability/measurement inference without inventing a claim it disavows.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: April PDF metadata conflicts with May proceedings publication
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Manuscript creation/modification can precede publication. Publisher/Crossref and repository identity are consistent; the exact repository bytes match the supplied file.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Two APA labels are proven independent human mechanisms
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: They are proposed clarification categories. The paper supplies no factor validation, participant results or unique causal identification.

cross_paper_learning.finding: Moral task structure and added morally relevant facts can legitimately change judgments. Distinguish a meaning-preserving frame test from a different action, intention or normative question.
Reflective questions can surface assumptions but can also embed false presuppositions. Asking why a choice contradicts core values assumes both an accurate core-value model and a true contradiction.

Population-distribution matching, individual preference recovery, factual correctness and normative validity differ. Neither a consistent choice nor a changed choice uniquely establishes moral alignment.
Sensemaking and coherent interpretation are useful aims but not automatic accuracy or performance gains. A cited theory and plausible interface are not an evaluated intervention.

deferred.term: CVR, APA and VRDS as three new behaviors
deferred.reason: These are proposed interface techniques/framework names rather than observed independent behaviors. Preserve their definitions and assumptions in study metadata; add only the two explicitly named clarification categories with conceptual status.

deferred.term: Moral stability as a validated latent metric
deferred.reason: No operational formula, test/retest reliability, equivalence test or validated mapping from choices to enduring values is supplied. More stability is not inherently more justified.

deferred.term: Five new ontology categories or ethical principles
deferred.reason: The five elicitation dimensions belong to the proposed simulation, not a new validated complete taxonomy. Preserve the existing project framework.

deferred.term: Later empirical follow-up as current evidence
deferred.reason: An author bibliography names Reflective Value Alignment Without Statistically Detectable Performance Loss. Its full text and findings were not read here. Preserve the pointer for a separate sequential review without importing results or duplicate credit.

limitations: Two related author-defined clarification categories added, not two established independent psychological mechanisms. Two existing records receive bounded conceptual evidence and five receive non-counted context. Catalogue becomes 799 records across eleven categories. Six ethical principles, seven evaluation criteria, stable IDs and unnumbered rows retained. No automatic harm links, forced citation quota, invented timeline, empirical improvement, raw-data replication, extra authorization layer or full-paper Markdown archive.
